kurz: How mortgage rates drive what buyers can pay, what US home price indexes measure and how to assess a local market with sales records rather than listings.

bloecke.md:
Two episodes shape how Americans think about home prices. From the peak in 2006 to the low in early 2012, the S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index fell by about 27%, and millions of homes went into foreclosure. From that low, the index more than doubled by mid-2022, with the fastest gains in 2020 and 2021, when mortgage rates hit record lows. Rising construction and land costs and a long period of too little homebuilding after 2008 pushed in the same direction, so the rise cannot be explained by speculation alone. Nor can it be explained by costs alone, because after 2022 prices rose much more slowly and fell in a number of regions, although building costs kept rising.

Both explanations are incomplete because they leave out the mortgage rate as a third factor. The rate determines what price a household can finance with a fixed monthly payment, and since 2022 it has changed more than incomes, rents and construction costs.

bloecke.titel: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate in the US, annual averages
bloecke.unter: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS). The weekly low was 2.65% on January 7, 2021, the high 7.79% on October 26, 2023. For the current weekly figure, see Freddie Mac or FRED (series MORTGAGE30US).

bloecke.md:
This lesson deliberately does not show a continuous price series up to 2026. Different indexes measure different things, and the figures for recent months are revised. The **S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller indices** use a repeat-sales method: they compare the prices of the same single-family homes sold twice, which removes most differences in size and location. They are published with a lag of about two months and as three-month moving averages. The **FHFA House Price Index** also uses repeat sales but covers only homes financed with mortgages bought or guaranteed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, so jumbo loans and cash purchases are missing. The **median sales price** published by the National Association of Realtors (NAR) is not an index at all: it moves when the mix of homes sold changes, for example when more large homes sell in summer.

You can retrieve the full series yourself, for example from FRED, the data service of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, and should not mix indexes with different methods in one chart. Every national index is an average across very different regions and property types. For your own purchase decision, it provides background information, not a basis for the decision.

## Mortgage rates and the price you can afford

Buyers rarely think in price per square foot; they think in monthly payments. Household income limits the payment, and lenders check it against the debt-to-income ratio. How much loan a payment can carry depends on the rate. The standard US mortgage is a fully amortizing 30-year fixed-rate loan: the payment stays the same for 30 years and repays the loan completely. The amount it can finance follows from the annuity formula.

bloecke.titel: Loan amount that a monthly payment of $2,000 can carry
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation, 30-year fixed rate, principal and interest only. Between the record low of January 2021 and the high of October 2023, the amount the same payment could finance fell by about 44%, although nothing had changed in the household.

bloecke.md: This calculation explains the market after 2022. Within less than two years, the same households could finance far less, but prices fell much less than financing capacity, and this was due to the supply side. Most US homeowners have a fixed-rate mortgage that they can usually repay at any time without a penalty. Those who had locked in 3% had little reason to sell and take out a new loan at 7%. This **lock-in effect** kept many existing homes off the market. Builders filled part of the gap, often by paying to buy down their buyers' mortgage rates. The result was a market with few transactions, but without a crash at the national level.

## Fixed rate, ARM and the refinancing option

In the US, the 30-year fixed rate is the norm, and most loans can be repaid early at any time. If rates fall, the borrower refinances; if they rise, the borrower keeps the old rate. This option has a price: 30-year rates are typically higher than 15-year rates. Adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs), such as a 7/6 ARM with a fixed rate for seven years and adjustments every six months thereafter, offer a lower initial rate and shift the interest rate risk to the borrower after the fixed period.

Mortgage rates follow the yield on 10-year Treasury notes plus a spread that compensates investors in mortgage-backed securities for the prepayment option and for credit risk. Forecasts of either are often far off in both directions. Only the structure is reliable: the longer the rate is fixed and the freer the borrower is to repay, the higher the rate.

## Price-to-rent ratio and rental yield

Any price level can be checked against the rent. The [[Price-to-rent ratio|price-to-rent ratio]] is the purchase price divided by the annual rent. It is the reciprocal of the gross yield: a ratio of 15 corresponds to 6.67% gross, a ratio of 25 to only 4%. The gross figure is only good for rough sorting, because closing costs and the costs that the landlord bears are missing.

The following calculation assumes a single-family house rented for $2,000 a month, that is, $24,000 a year. In the US, the largest cost item is often the property tax, which depends on the value of the property rather than on its size. The calculation assumes 1.1% of the price a year; actual rates range from well under 0.5% to more than 2%, depending on state and county. Other costs are homeowners insurance of $1,800, maintenance and repairs of $2,400 and 5% of the rent ($1,200) for vacancy and unpaid rent, without a property manager. On the cost side, buyer's closing costs of 3% of the price are added.

Net rental yield compared with the mortgage rate
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation from the table, before income tax and before financing. The 6.5% line is an assumption within the range of 30-year fixed rates in 2025; compare with the current rate. Only at a ratio of about 10 or below would the net yield exceed it.

bloecke.md: [[Leverage]] magnifies the difference between the property yield and the mortgage rate, in both directions. At a ratio of 18, the net yield in this calculation is 3.11%, while the assumed mortgage rate is 6.5%. Every borrowed dollar then lowers the return on equity instead of raising it. Once more than about 48% of the total cost is financed, the rent no longer covers the interest, and the purchase pays off only through appreciation, which nobody can guarantee. With the usual 20% down payment, that is the business model in most expensive metro areas. In markets with ratios near 10 or below, by contrast, the rent can carry the financing. Whether housing is expensive in general matters less than which part of the expected return comes from the rent and which part from hoped-for appreciation.

## Taxation of property and portfolio

A comparison with the stock market is incomplete as long as it is made before tax. Net rental income is taxed at ordinary rates, which reach 37% in 2026, but depreciation usually shelters a large part of it, and losses may be usable under the passive activity rules. Long-term capital gains and qualified dividends from a stock portfolio are taxed at 0%, 15% or 20%; for 2026, the 0% rate applies to taxable income up to $49,450 for single filers and $98,900 for married couples filing jointly. The 3.8% net investment income tax can apply to both.

On a sale, neither becomes tax-free after a holding period. The gain on a rental property includes recaptured depreciation, taxed at up to 25%, but a 1031 exchange can defer it indefinitely. A stock portfolio [[Tax deferral effect|defers gains]] simply by not being sold, and broad index funds rarely distribute capital gains. At death, both receive a step-up in basis. Your own home is treated much more generously: up to $250,000 of gain ($500,000 for married couples) is tax-free under 26 U.S.C. § 121 if you owned it and lived in it for two of the last five years, and interest on up to $750,000 of acquisition debt is deductible if you itemize. Depending on the holding period, the marginal rate and the use of these rules, the comparison can come out in favor of one investment or the other.

## Supply, regions and demographics

On the supply side, the US built too few homes for years after the 2008 crisis. The monthly New Residential Construction report of the Census Bureau shows building permits, housing starts and completions; permits lead starts and are the most useful early indicator. For existing homes, NAR reports the months' supply, the number of months it would take to sell the current inventory at the current sales pace. Around six months is traditionally considered a balanced market; far below that favors sellers, far above favors buyers.

Regionally, the US market consists of submarkets that have little to do with one another. In metro areas with job and population growth and restrictive zoning, rents can justify high prices. Where builders can add supply quickly, a building boom can push prices and rents down for a while, as happened in some Sun Belt metro areas after 2022. In regions whose population is shrinking, low prices are not a bargain, because they reflect a foreseeable letting problem. Insurance has become a regional factor of its own: in areas exposed to hurricanes, floods or wildfires, rising premiums and insurers leaving the market change what a property costs to own. This lesson deliberately contains no figures on migration and vacancy by county, because they quickly become outdated and are only meaningful locally. It is more important to know where to find them.

schritte.text: Deeds are recorded with the county recorder or clerk, and in most states the sale price can be read from the deed, from the transfer tax paid or from the assessor's sales file. Real estate agents can pull comparable sales (comps) from the multiple listing service (MLS). In non-disclosure states such as Texas and Utah, sale prices are not public record; there, appraisers and agents rely on the MLS.

The county assessor's website shows the assessed value, the split between land and improvements, the tax rate and the tax history of every parcel. Check whether the property will be reassessed at the purchase price; in California, for example, Proposition 13 resets the assessed value to the purchase price on a sale and then limits annual increases to 2%. The land and improvement split is also the usual starting point for depreciation.

schritte.titel: Compare advertised rents with market rents
schritte.text: Compare the rent used in the calculation with current listings for comparable units, with the rent the seller actually collects (ask for leases and bank statements) and with HUD's Fair Market Rents for the area. If the calculation uses a rent well above these, it may not be achievable.

schritte.titel: Record inventory and days on market
schritte.text: Count how many comparable homes are listed and how long they have been on the market. Listings do not show prices paid, but rising days on market and price cuts are early signs of room for negotiation.

The Census Bureau's population estimates and the American Community Survey show migration, age structure and incomes; its Building Permits Survey shows how much is being built. FEMA flood maps and insurance quotes show what the location will cost to insure. Rising permits with a stagnating population are a warning sign for rents.

Divide the purchase price by the achievable annual rent, then run the net calculation with property tax, insurance, maintenance and vacancy. Only the net result can be compared with the mortgage rate.

bloecke.md: The national index describes an average that does not apply to any single property. For a purchase decision, you need three local figures: the recorded prices of comparable sales, the achievable rent and your own mortgage rate. If the net rental yield is below that rate, the rest of the expected return depends on hoped-for appreciation. You can buy on that basis too, but you should be aware of it.

Home price indexes are nominal. If consumer prices rise faster than home prices, a property loses purchasing power although its dollar price goes up. After the 2006 peak, inflation made the real decline of US home prices considerably deeper than the nominal one, and in real terms it took years longer to regain the old peak.

For owner-occupiers, this matters less, because in return they save a rent that tends to rise with inflation; the consumer price index tracks this through owners' equivalent rent. For landlords, the point is central. A property protects against inflation only if rents can rise with other prices and if property taxes and insurance do not rise faster. Under rent stabilization or a statewide rent cap, this is restricted. Whether a property is an inflation hedge therefore depends on local law and local costs, not on real estate as such.

mitnehmen: The mortgage rate has the strongest influence on what buyers can pay: with the same monthly payment of $2,000, a 30-year loan shrinks from about $496,000 at 2.65% to about $278,000 at 7.79%.
Case-Shiller and FHFA indexes use repeat sales, the NAR median price does not; none of them describes a single local market.

The price-to-rent ratio is the reciprocal of the gross yield; only after closing costs, property tax, insurance, maintenance and vacancy does it produce a figure that can be compared with the mortgage rate.
If the net rental yield is below the mortgage rate, leverage works against the buyer, and the more debt is used, the more the return depends on appreciation.
Local conditions can be measured with recorded sales, assessor data, building permits and insurance costs, not with listings alone.

Repeat-sales index of the Federal Housing Finance Agency based on mortgages bought or guaranteed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. It leaves out jumbo loans and cash purchases.
Reluctance of homeowners with a low fixed mortgage rate to sell, because a new loan would cost much more. It reduces the supply of existing homes when rates rise.
Inventory of homes for sale divided by the monthly sales pace. Around six months is traditionally considered a balanced market.
Recent sales of similar properties nearby that appraisers and agents use to estimate value. They are based on recorded or MLS sale prices, not on asking prices.
